location: Kolargatan, Kvarnsveden industrial area, Borlänge, Dalarna
notes: One of Centrica's two Borlänge batteries. Omexom says both were running by the end of 2025; Centrica announced them online in April 2026. Satellite imagery shows a battery yard under construction on Kolargatan in the Kvarnsveden industrial area, directly behind Stafettvägen, which fits that description; it is a different yard from the two-container battery by Glans väg (probably KV 10-MW AB's). OpenStreetMap (via Open Infrastructure Map) tags this site as 'Bullerforsen BESS', operator Centrica, 20 MWh, start 2026, in Kvarnsveden west of the Dalälven between the Forshuvudforsen and Bullerforsen hydropower stations, which confirms it is the Kvarnsveden battery.

Borlänge's first large-scale solar park and energy storage: 4 MW of solar and a 4 MW battery, in operation. Separate from Borlänge Energi's 10 MW battery and Centrica's Bullerforsen and Romme. Energy capacity and start date not published.

notes: Jönköping Energi's smaller battery (4 MVA / 4 MWh), measured connected and operating in Energiforsk's 2026 power-quality study. Exact site and start date not published. Separate from the 10 MW Torsvik battery.

Listed as an operational battery in Flower's Q2 2026 report. Location and commissioning date not published.

Three batteries next to wind turbines on Varaslätten, 3 MW / 3 MWh in total.

notes: Roxem's first battery, connected in Växjö Energi's grid a short distance from Sandviksverket; Roxem said it was up and running, selling balancing services to Svenska kraftnät (Växjö Energi news, undated). Exact start date and energy capacity not published.
Built from reused EV batteries; installed spring 2023, in full operation from mid-summer 2023.
Battery added to the 12 MW solar park in 2022.

developer: Falkenklev Logistik (Soltech group is a co-owner; contractor Soltech Energy Solutions; control by CheckWatt)

notes: Soltech won a SEK 20 million order in February 2022 for Falkenklev's truck charging park at Stora Bernstorp with a 2 MW battery and a 1.5 ha solar park in Perstorp; CheckWatt was to run the battery for frequency services and trading. Soltech's reference case lists the Falkenklev energy storage project as completed in 2022 in Perstorp, so the battery may sit with the solar park rather than at the charging park. In April 2026 Åkeritidningen reported that four of Falkenklev's five charging stations (Arlöv, Helsingborg, Höör, Hörby, Perstorp) have battery storage. Soltech's February 2022 order release gave the battery as 2 MW; its reference case describes a 2 MW charging park, a 2 MWh battery park and a 1 MW solar park. Listed as 2 MW / 2 MWh (1-hour).

location: Habo, Jönköping County (at a receiving station)
notes: Habo Energi announced in July 2024 that it was investing in a 2 MW battery with Powerworks, for peak shaving, backup power and ancillary services; commissioning was planned for spring 2025 (Habo Energi on LinkedIn, 5 Jul 2024). Energiforsk's 2026 power-quality study measured it in operation: 2 MW / 2 MWh, Powerworks with Sungrow technology, connected at a receiving station.

Announced June 2023 for flexibility and ancillary services, to be connected around the turn of 2023/24. Foundation work was under way in September 2023 (Kvänum Energi, 'Energilager i Jung'). A site photo from October 2026 shows the finished, fenced installation with a permanent sign ('Flexibelt energilager 2 MW/2MWh'). Commissioning date not published. Separate from Kvänum Energi's three wind-turbine batteries (2025).

2 MW / 2 MWh battery sharing a grid connection with a 6 MWp solar park; described as newly operational and prequalified for Svenska kraftnät's ancillary services (PSW, 5 Jun 2026). Exact site not stated. Separate from Flower's Sköldinge battery and the BW ESS Katrineholm site.

developer: Swede Solar (owner); built by Soltech Energy Solutions, controlled by CheckWatt
location: PostNord TPL's logistics site at Malmölandet, outside Norrköping, Östergötland
notes: 2 MW battery owned by Swede Solar, which also owns the 6.3 MW rooftop solar; PostNord TPL uses the electricity and leases the site and its existing grid connection. In operation since April 2024, selling ancillary services to Svenska kraftnät via CheckWatt's control and letting the site use more of its own solar and cap peaks as electric-truck charging grows (PostNord TPL, 26 Aug 2024). Soltech reported the 4 MWh storage commissioned with a 6.5 MWp rooftop system on 31 Oct 2024.

online: Installed late 2021; in ancillary-service operation from March 2026
notes: Container battery (Alfen, Samsung cells) installed with Fortum in late 2021 to keep Boo Energi within its grid subscription (Processnet, 8 Nov 2021; Boo Energi energy storage page). Boo Energi's 2025 annual report says its energy storage went into operation in March 2026 for the ancillary services market; it does not say whether that is the same unit.

developer: Catena (built by Takorama Elteknik, part of Soltech)
location: Catena logistics property, Borås, Västra Götaland
notes: Ordered by logistics property company Catena in November 2023, with work from 2024: a 1.5 MW battery with a 1 MW rooftop solar system (about 5,000 m²), new switchgear, a high-voltage connection and a transformer station. Takorama reported the project completed in autumn 2025 (Soltech on LinkedIn). Separate from Borås Energi och Miljö's and Ra Energy's batteries. Energy capacity not published.

developer: Alfredsson Transport (battery from Polarium, chargers from Kempower)
location: Alfredsson Transport's new depot, Norrköping, Östergötland
notes: 1.2 MW / 2.2 MWh Polarium battery with a 400 kWp solar park at an electric-truck charging depot; in September 2025 the depot demonstrated megawatt charging of two trucks at once (Polarium, 22 Sep 2025). Exact start date not published.

location: Ra Energy's premises, Borås, Västra Götaland
notes: Installed and commissioned for ancillary services. 1.44 MWh per Stella Futura's case page (now redirected to Polarium, which bought Stella Futura in 2025).

location: Probably the Timboholm bus depot, Skövde, Västra Götaland
notes: Listed among Sparq Technology's delivered references as a 1.2 MW / 3 MWh battery in Skövde, dated December 2024. Indoor battery cabinets for ancillary services and electric-bus charging, so probably at a bus depot rather than one of Skövde's outdoor battery-park permits. Sparq lists it among its installed Swedish systems (Sparq, 23 Sep 2026). Skövde Energi's 2024 annual report says three of its four customer-connected batteries were finished and the fourth, at the Timboholm bus depot where Skövde's electric city buses charge, was not yet complete; this is very likely that battery. Owner and site not confirmed by Sparq.

SunStreet runs a combined 1.4 MW solar park and 1 MW / 2 MWh battery in Falkenberg; listed among its completed projects as in operation. Start date not published. Separate from Primrock's Falkenberg battery.

Hybrid with the hydropower plant, delivering frequency services to Svenska kraftnät. Installation finished summer 2022 per LT ('Batterier i Hissmofors ska rädda elnätet från störningar', 26 Nov 2022); Energiföretagen (May 2023) and Jämtkraft's Hissmofors page both say it was built in 2021, Jämtkraft's first battery plant.
Primora's first self-owned battery: a standalone system providing grid support services. Listed as in operation since 2025.

location: Landafors hydropower plant, Ljusnan, Bollnäs, Gävleborg
notes: Hydro-battery hybrid: 48 batteries totalling 1 MW / 250 kWh, being installed at Fortum's Landafors hydropower plant in April 2021 (Fortum). Start date not published.

Precendia delivered and commissioned two 1 MWh / 500 kW units (1 MW / 2 MWh in total) with control and monitoring, for ancillary services. Commissioned in early summer 2026; since then it has earned strong ancillary-service revenue for Lodjursparken's owner (Precendia project page; LinkedIn, Oct 2026). Owner and location not published.

Farm battery of 1 MW / 1.1 MWh, installed 2024 by Enermont of Hässleholm. Used to store energy when demand is low and use it at peaks, to cut energy costs and power peaks and improve reliability; Enermont also lists it under ancillary services (Enermont reference page). Battery supplier and grid owner not stated.
SunStreet runs a 1.5 MW solar park with a 1 MW / 2 MWh battery; listed among its completed projects as in operation. Start date not published.

SunStreet owns and runs a 2.0 MW solar park with a 1 MW / 2 MWh battery; listed among its completed projects as in operation. Start date not published. Separate from Uddevalla Energi's battery at Lillesjöverket.

SunStreet's 6 MWh energy storage at Nödesta, described as completed and strengthening the Stockholm region's grid. Power and start date not published. SunStreet said in late 2025 (LinkedIn, after taking over three solar and battery parks from Svensson Enterprises in a deal worth just under SEK 100 million) that it manages seven energy sites in SE3 and SE4 with 10 MW of solar and 21.3 MW of storage in total. With Borlänge (4 MW), Falkenberg, Tjörn and Uddevalla (1 MW each) known, about 14 MW is left for Nödesta and Trångfors, consistent with roughly 1-hour systems of about 6 MW and 8 MW, but not confirmed per site.

location: Former landfill at Rottneros mill, outside Sunne, Värmland
notes: Battery of up to 8.9 MWh next to a 4,284-panel solar park (about 2.6 GWh a year), described as Värmland's largest. Batteries supplied by Powerworks, panels by Nordic Solar; whole investment about SEK 90 million. Inaugurated 10 April 2025, later than the end of August 2024 first planned (Börsvärlden, Feb 2024; Papper & Massa, Apr 2025). Power not published.

Four battery containers (8 MWh) delivered November 2024 next to the 16.2 MW hydropower station, energised at the turn of 2024/25. By March 2025 it had been tested and was awaiting Svenska kraftnät's approval to sell ancillary services (Mälarenergi press release, 14 Mar 2025). VLT (22 Feb 2026) describes the battery as already built. The planned solar park (about 5 MW on 5 ha, about 7.5 GWh a year) got its building permit in February 2026 and still needs approval from Västerås municipal council; it would make the site a hydro-solar-battery hybrid park on one grid connection. Power not published. A 5 MW solar park at the site got its building permit in February 2026, making it a hydro + solar + battery hybrid on one grid connection, run by the Mälarenergi–SunStreet joint company (VLT, 22 Feb 2026); the four containers arrived in November 2024 (VLT, 21 Nov 2024). SunStreet said in late 2025 (LinkedIn, after taking over three solar and battery parks from Svensson Enterprises in a deal worth just under SEK 100 million) that it manages seven energy sites in SE3 and SE4 with 10 MW of solar and 21.3 MW of storage in total. With Borlänge (4 MW), Falkenberg, Tjörn and Uddevalla (1 MW each) known, about 14 MW is left for Nödesta and Trångfors, consistent with roughly 1-hour systems of about 6 MW and 8 MW, but not confirmed per site.

OX2 lists it as under construction next to the 189 MW Fageråsen wind farm, with the project commissioned in 2028. Investment decision July 2026 with the battery due at the end of 2027 (Sälennytt); 209 MWh per Trina Storage's supply agreement. In early October 2026 OX2 showed about 100 landowners and neighbours the construction site; the wind and storage park is to start delivering to the grid in 2028 (OX2 on LinkedIn).

Bought from Arise in 2024; connects to the Kölvallen wind farm substation (Arise). Flower expected commercial operation for its three Swedish projects in September–October 2026. Monsson's first battery in Sweden, 30 MW / 60 MWh, developed and made in the EU. Bought from Neoen fully permitted in May 2025 with construction set to start June 2025. An inauguration with guided tours is set for 22 October 2026 (invitation shared by Monsson's partner NURI on LinkedIn, Oct 2026); listed as operational once that is confirmed.

Listed in Flower's 2025 year-end report; exact site not published. Separate from Nordic Solar's 10 MW Södertälje battery as far as the sources show. Flower's Q2 2026 report (27 Aug 2026) says all three Swedish projects under construction are progressing well and expected to reach commercial operation in Q4 2026.

location: Not published (project company Skolmyra Batteripark AB)
notes: Listed in Flower's 2025 year-end report; location not published. Flower's Q2 2026 report (27 Aug 2026) says all three Swedish projects under construction are progressing well and expected to reach commercial operation in Q4 2026.

GoodPower sold the 7 MW / 15 MWh project to CA Batteribalans (CA Energi) in June 2025; GoodPower lists it as under construction. Separate from the Port of Trelleborg's own battery.

Third of Trollhättan Energi's three batteries. The 2025 annual report says it will be commissioned in 2026, somewhat delayed by an appealed building permit. Under construction in June 2026, next to the Ladugårdsbyn homes, with neighbours objecting (TTELA, 28 Jun 2026). Size assumes an even split of the 9 MW / 11.2 MWh total; not published per site.

Two battery systems totalling 1.44 MW built from reused electric-car batteries. Norwegian company ReCube hired Omexom (VINCI Energies) for design, groundwork, earthing and electrical installation, with sister company Actemium on the electrical work; the systems are connected to a local substation and a new switchgear. Work started in September 2026 and the systems are delivered at different times, with completion expected in spring 2027 (Omexom press release, 7 Oct 2026; also Energinyheter). Energy capacity not published.
Size not published.

Battery container of 2 MWh at the municipal company's recycling centre, behind the fence opposite the weighbridge. It arrived before summer 2026; as of 9 Sep 2026 testing and permit work remained before commissioning. Paired with 700 solar panels on three roofs (in operation since 2025); an AI system will decide when to use or sell the energy, and the battery is meant to keep the site running for a full day during a power cut (Hässleholm Miljö, 9 Sep 2026). Installer Enermont posted on LinkedIn in Jan 2026 that preparatory cabling, cabinet and groundwork was under way. Power not published.
Size not published.

developer: Trelleborgs Hamn (installed by Takorama Elteknik, part of Soltech)
notes: Contract signed January 2026 for design and installation of a 4 MWh energy storage, to raise the port's self-sufficiency and meet coming EU requirements for shore power to larger ships. Commissioning expected during 2026. By 29 September 2026 the battery was installed in the port area, with a test run due within a month before operation; it will cut peaks when several ships use shore power and store the port's own wind power (Trelleborgs Hamn). Power and order value not published.

location: Regumatorp 2:16 and part of municipal Regumatorp 2:5, Skultorp area, Skövde, Västra Götaland
notes: Four battery containers (59 m²) got a building permit in June 2025; the battery, inverters and a substation were then built partly in a different spot than permitted and got a retroactive permit in October 2025 (Skövde building committee, 5 Jun and 23 Oct 2025). Vallda Energi lists energy storage sites in Skultorp and Kådene, so this is very likely the Skultorp battery permit mentioned by Skaraborgs Allehanda (May 2025, Sep 2026). Operation not confirmed; size not published.

location: Tuve, Göteborg (probably the meadows by Tuve substation)
notes: Ingrid listed Tuve as under construction with commissioning expected in 2026 (Dec 2025). Göteborg refused a first application in early 2024 because the land was farmland, then approved a second one; about a dozen neighbours appealed and the county board was reviewing the decision. Not confirmed that this is the same site. Size not published.

notes: 10 MWh battery in a 24 MW solar park (about 25 ha), connected to Vattenfall's grid. Used to shift output to high-price hours and for ancillary services. Power not published.

Environmental permit from the county board's environmental assessment delegation in Dalarna (decision announced by the county board on 25 May 2026; Korkia, 26 Jun 2026) for a 150 MWp solar park with a 150 MW / 600 MWh (4-hour) battery, about 150 GWh of solar a year. Korkia says it has a secured grid connection and is working towards ready-to-build status. No construction or operation dates published.

location: At the Timmersdala switchyard (Stora Stolan 3:1 / Timmersdala), about 12 km north-west of Skövde, Västra Götaland
notes: Neoen's third Swedish battery, about 100 MW on 1.8 ha next to the transformer station, chosen because the area needs frequency stabilisation. Consultation notice May 2025, building permit applied June 2025 and granted September 2025 (Skövde building committee minutes, 23 Oct 2025); an appeal was rejected on 17 February 2026, so the permit stands. The Timmersdala application covers just over 120 containers (Skaraborgs Allehanda, 10 May 2025). No construction or commissioning date published; energy capacity not published.

The building permit with legal force covers 200 MWh. In April 2026 Ingrid said it was reapplying with updated specifications to reach 400 MWh (4-hour), which would make it Sweden's largest battery, with construction from 2026 and full operation in 2028. The Sept 2026 Mirova investment report still gives 200 MWh and ready-to-build 2027, so 200 MWh is used here until the larger permit is confirmed.

Standalone battery (not paired with wind or solar), per BayWa's preliminary site layout dated 24 Oct 2024, which was circulated to neighbours for comment during the permit process. Building permit granted Mar 2025 for about 1 ha; detailed design and grid connection work under way. BayWa plans commissioning in 2034. Energy capacity not published.

Building permit granted Dec 2024. In October 2023 BayWa said the site, up to 8,000 m² in the Mon area about 10 km west of Ed, could hold up to 75 MWh and be in place during 2026, depending on grid capacity (Dalslänningen, 24 Oct 2023). BayWa now gives 75 MW; energy capacity not confirmed.

developer: Landinfra Energy (project company Knäred Batteripark AB)
location: Lagered 12:1 (municipal land), south-east of Knäred, Laholm, Halland
notes: About 70 MW of container batteries on about 2 ha. Building permit applied for Q4 2024 and in legal force from spring 2025; technical design and grid connection under review with the grid owner (Landinfra project page). Laholm municipality approved the land lease in August 2023 and road access agreements in March 2026 (minutes, 10 Mar 2026, § 52). Separate from Primora's 1 MW Knäred battery. Energy capacity and timeline not published.

About 70 MW on about 4 ha. Neoen held the consultation and got its permits during 2025; in 2026 it is in talks with the regional grid company about the connection (Neoen project page). Separate from Nybro Energi's own 5 MW and 12 MW batteries. Energy capacity and timeline not published.

location: Häggatorp 10:1, south-west of Kallinge, Ronneby, Blekinge
notes: About 70 MW of container batteries on about 2 ha. Building permit applied for Q4 2024 and in legal force from spring 2025; technical design and grid connection under review with the grid owner (Landinfra project page). Energy capacity and timeline not published.
Building permit granted May 2025 for about 1 ha; detailed design and grid connection work under way. BayWa plans commissioning in 2029. Energy capacity not published.

Building permit granted April 2026 for up to about 73 containers, about 40 expected (1,130 m²), plus a substation, near a large overhead power line. Investment about SEK 300 million, for arbitrage and frequency services. Awaiting grid owner Ellevio before a connection agreement; connection estimated mid-2029 because of long transformer lead times. A solar park is planned next to it around 2030 (Filipstads Tidning, 18 Apr 2026). Separate from Axpo's Filipstad project.

location: Undeveloped land west of Emmaboda, Kalmar County
notes: Approved by Kalmar County Administrative Board (12:6 consultation); building permits still to be applied for. The site could hold up to 200 MW of batteries, but grid limits may cut it to about 40 MW, the figure used here; target full operation early 2028 (SVT, 6 Mar 2024). No later update found. Separate from Flower's small Emmaboda battery.

location: Sjöhagsvägen by the CHP plant, Västerås
notes: Own investment; 12 containers of 5 MWh, to even out power peaks and serve as a resource during larger outages. Cut from an earlier 100 MWh plan (SVT, Nov 2023), with a smaller footprint than first planned. Press release (16 Mar 2026) says complete end of 2026; SVT (31 Mar 2026) said spring 2027. Mälarenergi's board minutes trace the project: a letter of intent with Polar Capacity in late 2023; a June 2024 decision to develop the battery park at the CHP plant in-house (project M230002), possibly in its own subsidiary; an investment frame in August 2024; in October 2024 the regional grid owner Vattenfall would not allow a battery within 100 m of the existing switchgear because of fire risk, so other sites were studied; in April 2025 the CEO decided to invest about SEK 276 million (below the SEK 500 million frame) in a turnkey plant connected to the 130 kV grid that also replaces the diesel backup power; delays were reported in December 2024 and September 2025; and in December 2025 the building permit was in place and the project entering a more intensive phase (Mälarenergi board minutes, Västerås stad). Construction start date not stated.

developer: Galileo Empower (project company Hultsfreds Bess AB)
location: Nyhagen industrial area (Transportgatan/Industrigatan), Hultsfred, Kalmar County
notes: Galileo's project page lists the Hultsfred energy store as 'building permit granted', up to 25 MW, made up of battery modules on about 5,000 m², to stabilise the grid. The permit was granted on 24 Aug 2023 (61 battery units in 15 groups, 8 transformers and a control building), Galileo's first battery permit in Sweden (Vimmerby Tidning, 1 Sep 2023); Galileo bought the 5,130 m² municipal plot in spring 2024. Construction had not started by Sep 2025 because Galileo was still waiting for E.ON's grid study and connection date; the municipality extended the building deadline to 21 Sep 2028, and Vimmerby Tidning (8 Oct 2025) reported that a new building permit would be needed. Energy capacity not published.

EnBW plans five battery containers with 25 MW in total at Storrisberget, built before its planned wind turbines, on a site already prepared for industrial use (Sveriges Radio P4 Jämtland, 6 Jul 2024). A building permit application for 'BESS Storrisberget' was on Ragunda's building committee agenda on 27 Jun 2024, and Jämtlands Tidning later reported a building permit for a battery store in Krångede, very likely the same project. The Storrisberget wind farm was later stopped over reindeer herding; whether the battery is going ahead on its own is not confirmed. Energy capacity not published.
Up to 25 MW battery with 34 ha solar park; permit granted by Länsstyrelsen Halland 2026.

location: Kristianstad, Skåne (site not published; E.ON grid)

Site per Alingsås Tidning. No confirmation it was built. Energy capacity not published.

location: Malmö, Skåne (site not published; 10 kV connection to E.ON)
notes: Huawei LFP system of 15 MW / 70 MWh. Construction and commissioning dates not published.
